label: Piglet
description: A very small animal being ever so brave about the route.
direction: Speak in Piglet's small, soft, high and slightly quavering voice: timid, sweet and polite, nervous but trying very hard to be brave. Keep the direction word clear.
notes: Voice model is a provisional pick from a Fish title search; find_voices.py auditions it and ship_roster.py build writes the final pick here. Character lives on greetings and road prompts; turns stay plain.

rights.source_work: Winnie the Pooh and the Blustery Day and later Disney Winnie the Pooh films
rights.author: The Walt Disney Company (character created by A. A. Milne)
rights.pd_basis: Partial at most. Piglet as written in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh (1926) is in the US public domain, but the voice cloned here is Disney's animated performance, first heard in 1968, which remains under copyright, and Disney holds live trademarks in the name. The public-domain presets, written from the book alone, are pooh, eeyore and tigger.
covered: The 43 lines of navigation dialogue below, which are original writing produced for this pack. A few greetings and alerts deliberately echo the character's well-known personality and catchphrases; those are the rights holder's, not ours.
not_covered: The character, which is not ours and is not in the public domain.
The character's name and the Winnie the Pooh name, which are live Disney trademarks.
Any recorded voice performance of the character, by any performer.

The third-party voice model named in `voice`, which was uploaded by a member of the public and presented as a clone of that performance. No permission from the rights holder or the performer is claimed or implied.
Any commercial use. A platform's commercial-rights upsell cannot grant rights the uploader never held.
rights.notes: This preset is in copyright and says so. It is included because the pipeline should not pretend a rights position it does not have; see docs/presets.md before publishing anything built from it. The public-domain presets are pooh, eeyore and tigger.

lines.in_quarter_mile: In a quarter of a mile.
lines.in_1000_meters: In one kilometer. Oh my, that's rather close.
lines.in_1500_meters: In one point five kilometers. I'm being brave.
lines.in_one_mile: In one mile. Oh, I do hope that's not too far.
lines.start_drive_1: Oh, hello! It's me, Piglet. Shall we go together?
lines.start_drive_2: Oh, d-dear. A whole drive? Well, I'll be brave. Let's go.
lines.start_drive_3: Hello, friend. Everything is friendlier with two.
lines.start_drive_4: I've packed some haycorns, just in case. Off we go!
lines.start_drive_5: Pooh says I'm braver than I think. Let's find out!
lines.start_drive_6: Good morning! Or afternoon. Either way, let's go.
lines.start_drive_7: A very small animal can still read a map. Let's go!
lines.start_drive_8: Oh my, the open road. It's ever so big. Hold on tight.
lines.start_drive_9: Is that a heffalump? No? Oh, good. Let's be off, then.
lines.exit_left: Take the exit on the left.
lines.exit_right: Take the exit on the right.
lines.u_turn: Make a U turn. Oh dear, oh dear. It's quite all right.
lines.arrived: We're here! Oh, I was ever so brave, wasn't I?
lines.exit_fifth: take the fifth exit. Oh my!
lines.exit_sixth: take the sixth exit. Steady now.
lines.exit_seventh: take the seventh exit. Round and round, like a blustery day.
lines.traffic_ahead: Traffic ahead. Oh dear. We'll just wait quietly, then.
lines.accident_ahead: An accident ahead. Oh my. Please go very carefully.
lines.hazard_ahead: A hazard ahead! Oh, d-dear, do watch out!
lines.speed_camera_ahead: Speed camera ahead. Let's go nice and slowly.
lines.red_light_camera_ahead: Red light camera ahead. Best to stop, I think.
lines.police_ahead: Police ahead. Oh my. Let's be very, very good.
lines.reroute_chime: Oh, d-dear, we've gone astray. Not to worry. A new way!
